event.text: Does the numbness or tingling extend into your forearm or upper arm, or is it only in your hand?
event.why: Distribution (distal hand only vs. extending proximally) helps distinguish localized compression like carpal tunnel from cervical radiculopathy or other proximal nerve involvement, which affects routing and urgency.

event.text: I recommend a Counsel clinician review your hand symptoms in this thread, with a same-day service-hours target. Numbness and tingling in one hand that's worse at night is often nerve compression at the wrist, but the pattern needs a clinician's assessment. If weakness, face drooping, trouble speaking or new numbness comes on suddenly, call 911 immediately. If your hand instead gradually becomes weaker or clumsier over days, seek in-person care that same day.
